newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Eight Pakistani tribe members killed in ambush.
newsitem.headline: Eight Pakistani tribe members killed in ambush.

text.p: Eight members of a Pakistani tribe were shot dead in an ambush on Tuesday in the southwestern province of Baluchistan, the official APP news agency said.

It quoted provincial home department secretary Ashraf Nasar as saying all eight Kakar tribe members, who were driving in a pickup truck, died instantly in the attack by gunmen on a highway near Qila Abdullah town, 75 km (45 miles) northwest of the provincial capital Quetta.
A government statement said the attack stemmed from a blood feud between Kakars and the rival Ghaibizai tribe, who have accused each other in the past of revenge killings.
Law enforcement agencies were sent to the area to control the situation, Nasar said.
Blood feuds are often settled by violence in the predominantly tribal society of Baluchistan, which borders Afghanistan and Iran and is Pakistan's largest but least populated province.
